text:
Aydar Suniev is a 21-year-old who came the long way: Kazan, then the BCHL with Penticton, then a season at UMass, then Calgary as a third-round pick in 2023. He has four goals in 17 games in his first real NHL run, which already beats what most people expected.

The finishing is running ahead of the chances. He's shooting 16.7%, above the 13% we'd expect, and he has about one more goal than his chances say. That's a normal hot start for a young forward, not a warning sign. His chance rate is decent for 13 minutes a night, and the Flames are a bit better with him than without at five on five.

The bigger thing to watch is the role. His minutes dipped below 10 in two of his last four games, 8.8 against the Rangers, and a young winger on a team with Matvei Gridin and Adam Klapka pushing for the same ice doesn't get many free shifts. What keeps him in the lineup is getting to the net on the nights the puck isn't going in.
